items.title: Basic concept of scalars and vectors

source_refs.note: Unnumbered opening section (PDF 23, printed 20); catalogue key u-basic-concept-of-scalars-and-vectors. The learning objectives (PDF 22) are not reproduced.

blocks.text: Scalars and vectors are basic concepts in physics. Many problems in physics require us to distinguish between scalar and vector quantities in order to apply the correct mathematical and conceptual approaches. Understanding scalars and vectors helps us to grasp how physics applies to real-world situations, such as calculating the total distance travelled (a scalar) or determining the magnitude and direction of a force (a vector). Learning these concepts develops critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

This chapter is primarily concerned with vector algebra and its application to uniformly accelerated motion in a straight line, the motion of freely falling bodies in a uniform gravitational field, projectile motion, and the interaction between objects in one and two dimensions.

blocks.caption: What the chapter covers
rows: scalars, vectors, components, scalar and vector products (2.1 to 2.3)
equations of motion, motion under gravity (2.4, 2.5)
momentum, impulse, elastic and inelastic collisions, rocket propulsion (2.7 to 2.12)

blocks.prompt: Why does physics need two kinds of quantity rather than one?
blocks.explanation: Some quantities are fully described by a number with a unit, like the distance walked; others need a direction as well, like the force on a door, and adding or multiplying them has to respect that direction. Keeping scalars and vectors apart tells us which mathematics to apply.

items: Scalars and vectors need different mathematics; this chapter covers vector algebra, uniformly accelerated straight-line motion, free fall, projectiles and collisions in one and two dimensions.
